claims.statement: WHO guidance says effective procurement and inventory management should track stock, expiry dates, and reordering to prevent service interruptions, stockouts, and wastage of testing materials.
EMA's European Shortages Monitoring Platform collects medicine supply, demand, and availability data and supports machine-to-machine submissions from national and industry systems.

contrary_evidence: Wholesaler ERP systems already provide basic reorder and expiry functions for larger customers.
Independent clinics may have insufficient inventory discipline to supply reliable on-hand data.

economics.acquisition_route: Select one consumable class, import historical orders and manual stock counts for 10-20 clinics under one wholesaler, and test forecast and expiry precision offline.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 3000 clinic sites at 200 PLN monthly net revenue yield 7.2m PLN ARR before shared savings; at 30% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity is about 5.2m PLN in year 6-9. Retained earnings are not added separately.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-16 hours weekly, with regulated logistics and quality decisions left to licensed channel partners.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 68-80% after integrations, support, and savings verification, with no inventory on the startup's balance sheet.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 20000-45000 PLN wholesaler onboarding recovered within 8-14 months at 25-50 paid clinic sites.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 150-300 PLN per clinic monthly plus 10-20% of verified avoided expiry loss; regulated logistics remain with the wholesaler.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every order and stock count refreshes the service; annual retention follows the wholesaler relationship if avoided waste is visible.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-customer demand patterns, lead times, expiry outcomes, and substitute availability improve forecasts and pooling
fingerprint.customer: Independent clinics and testing sites buying expiring medical consumables through a wholesaler
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Medical wholesalers embed the service in the portal used for every repeat order
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Inventory forecast, expiry alert, compliant return or transfer orchestration, and shared-savings analytics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Wholesaler or clinic pays per site monthly, plus an optional share of independently verified avoided write-offs
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Stock approaches expiry, consumption deviates from plan, or a reorder risks either shortage or surplus

founder_fit: Forecasting and anomaly detection use the founder's data-science strengths.
Wholesaler distribution reaches many small buyers through an existing ordering habit.
A software pilot using exports avoids inventory ownership and stays within capital limits.
risks: Product transfers or returns may violate distribution, traceability, temperature, or reimbursement rules.
Bad forecasts can create stockouts that interrupt care.
Lot and expiry data may be unavailable at clinic level.

structure.control_point: Lot-level demand, expiry, substitute, and compliant disposition workflow across buyers
structure.critical_dependency: Accurate lot-level data and a legally compliant wholesaler-managed reverse-logistics path

thesis: Embed demand forecasting, lot-expiry alerts, reorder suggestions, and compliant return-or-transfer workflows into a medical wholesaler's ordering portal for independent clinics and testing sites. The wholesaler repeatedly sees purchasing while customers supply consumption and on-hand data. The service prevents stockouts and expired kits, and can earn a subscription plus a share of independently verified avoided waste; it never enables unlicensed resale or bypasses required cold-chain controls.
title: Wholesaler-Coordinated Expiry Exchange for Clinic Supplies
uncertainties: Which diagnostic kits or consumables have enough expiry loss and legal transfer flexibility for a first wedge?
Can avoided waste be measured against a credible baseline?
Will the wholesaler prefer higher inventory sales over leaner customer stock?
